title: tree-sitter-renpy: [var] interpolation brackets inside screen-language string breaks tokenizer
description: Found in bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 13 (full-surface regression suite), 2026-08-16. A screen-language string containing Ren'Py's [var]-style text interpolation syntax (e.g. text "Trust: [trust]" inside a screen block) breaks the tokenizer -- the string/property grammar doesn't correctly handle the [...] interpolation markup inside screen-language string values the way it's documented to for say-statement dialogue text (say_statement's text field decomposes interpolation spans per Task 4's design). Task 13 worked around it by avoiding [var] interpolation in its screen-language sample content (documented inline in src/test/treeSitterRenpy.test.ts) rather than fixing the grammar, since that's out of scope for a consumer-side test. Recommended fix when picked up: investigate whether screen-language string values need the same interpolation-decomposition treatment as say_statement's text field, or whether a narrower lexer fix suffices.

title: tree-sitter-renpy: leading blank line before first statement produces spurious top-level ERROR
description: First flagged during bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 8 (error-recovery hardening) as an out-of-scope concern (not one of Task 8's 3 named hot-path cases), then independently re-encountered in Task 13's full-surface regression suite (2026-08-16), confirming it's a real, recurring issue affecting realistic .rpy content, not just a synthetic edge case. A leading blank line at the very start of a file/block produces a spurious ERROR node because nothing in _statement accepts a bare top-level _newline token. Task 13 worked around it by avoiding leading blank lines in its fixture (documented inline in src/test/treeSitterRenpy.test.ts) rather than fixing the grammar, since that's out of scope for a consumer-side test. Recommended fix when picked up: add a _statement alternative (or extras-level handling) that accepts a bare leading newline, consistent with how real .rpy files commonly start with a blank line after a comment header.

title: tree-sitter-renpy: add corpus regression test for say-statement followed by separate with_statement
description: Follow-up from bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 8 fix-round re-review, 2026-08-16. Task 8's fix made say_statement's trailing $._newline optional (to harden the no-Enter-yet mid-typing hot-path case), which required adding a conflicts:[[$.say_statement]] + prec.dynamic(1,...) declaration to disambiguate an inline with-clause on a say-statement from a separate top-level with_statement on the following line. The re-reviewer confirmed this mechanism is narrowly scoped (only affects say_statement, since scene/show/hide retain mandatory newlines) and verified correct via ad-hoc tree-sitter parse -r testing, but flagged that this exact case -- 'eileen "hi"' followed on the next line by a standalone 'with dissolve' -- has ZERO committed corpus regression coverage. Since prec.dynamic resolves ambiguity silently (no ERROR node if it picks the wrong parse), a future grammar change could start incorrectly merging a legitimate separate with_statement into the preceding say_statement with no test failure to catch it. Recommended fix: add a corpus case (in test/corpus/error-recovery.txt or test/corpus/say-statements.txt) asserting the say_statement and the following with_statement remain two distinct sibling statement nodes.

title: tree-sitter-renpy: define/default/image value fields break on quoted strings containing '#'
description: Follow-up from bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 7 code review, 2026-08-16. The shared opaque expression regex (/[^\n#:]+/ in grammar.js) unconditionally excludes '#' since '#' starts a Ren'Py comment. Task 7 fixed this for style_property_statement's value field by adding alias($.string, $.expression) as an alternative so quoted strings (e.g. background "#333") parse correctly even when they contain '#'. The same latent bug exists, unaddressed, in define_statement/default_statement/image_statement's value fields (plain field('value', $.expression)) -- e.g. 'define BG = "#333"' would hit the same single-quote-char-then-ERROR failure the Task 7 fix diagnosed. Left alone in Task 7 since patching it was out of that task's stated scope and risked regressing Task 3/4's settled corpus tests. Recommended fix when picked up: apply the same choice(alias($.string, $.expression), $.expression) pattern to define_statement/default_statement/image_statement's value fields (grammar.js, established alias pattern already used at multiple sites: alias(/-?[0-9]+/, $.expression), alias($._bare_expr_head, $.expression), alias($._at_expr_blob, $.expression)).

title: tree-sitter-renpy: at_expr/attributes narrowed to identifier lists, can't parse Transform(...) calls
description: Follow-up from bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 4 (say/python/scene/show statements) code review, 2026-08-16. scene_statement/show_statement's at_expr field (grammar.js, _at_expr_blob) is narrowed to a comma-separated identifier list, matching the established _for_target_blob/_parameter_blob opaque-blob precedent from Task 3. This means a common real Ren'Py idiom -- 'show eileen happy at Transform(xzoom=2.0)' or any at-clause using a function call rather than a bare named transform -- will not parse correctly (the blob regex doesn't handle nested parens/commas inside a call). Not exercised by any of Task 4's required corpus tests, so not currently caught by the test suite. Recommended when picked up: either broaden _at_expr_blob to a balanced-paren-aware regex/rule, or accept the limitation and document it, similar to the parameter_list nested-paren caveat noted in Task 3's review.

title: tree-sitter-renpy: comment as first line of a block can't establish indentation
description: Follow-up from bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 2 (external indentation scanner) code review, 2026-08-16. The scanner's comment-line exclusion fix (Important #2) correctly stops interior comment lines from spuriously triggering INDENT/DEDENT, but as a side effect a comment as the literal FIRST line of a block's body can never establish that block's _indent, since _indent is mandatory immediately after _newline (before repeat1($._statement)) and comments are deliberately excluded from indent-stack participation. This is a real, common Ren'Py pattern: 'label start:\n    # intro\n    "Hello"'. Not reachable/blocking during Task 2 (scanner infra only, _block not wired into any real rule yet) -- flagged as a tracked follow-up for whichever of Tasks 3-7 first wires _block into label/if/menu/screen. Recommended fix direction (per reviewer): evaluate making 'comment' an extra token (tree-sitter-python's own approach) at that point, rather than a _statement alternative.

title: Translation Dashboard: fall back to tl/ file instead of source when string is untranslated
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open the Translation Dashboard for a project with detected languages.
2. Filter by Untranslated status.
3. Click a string row (or its per-language badge).

## Expected
Navigate into the corresponding tl/<lang>/ file so the user can add the translation.

## Actual (before fix)
Silently opened the main script with no explanation, even though a tl/<lang>/ folder existed for the project.

## Fix
Added deriveTlFilePath() (inverse of deriveSourceFilePath) in renpyTranslationParser.ts. Row click and per-language badge now navigate into the tl/<lang>/ file when it exists (even without a matched entry for that specific string), or toast a 'generate translations first' warning and fall back to source when the tl file doesn't exist at all. Language badges are no longer disabled for missing translations -- they're now clickable to trigger this same navigation.
design: Reused existing deriveSourceFilePath()'s tl/<lang>/ path convention; added the inverse deriveTlFilePath(). Wired addToast (already threaded through useTabContentRenderer for other tabs) into TranslationDashboard as an optional prop.
acceptance_criteria: Row click and per-language badge click on an untranslated string open tl/<lang>/<file>.rpy when that file exists in blocks[]; toast shown either way; falls back to source only when no tl file exists for that language at all. All tests pass, 0 lint errors.
close_reason: Fixed in this session: added deriveTlFilePath(), attemptOpenUntranslated() fallback in TranslationDashboard, enabled per-language badges. 2306 tests pass, 0 lint errors.

Added regression tests across all three hook test files (2299 total tests green, tsc clean). Remaining steps: (1) send script to VO service and get timed audio back, (2) capture b-roll clips for each visual cue -- Playwright video recording against DemoProject is a good fit since it reuses the same app-driving infrastructure as docs/capture_screenshots.js, (3) source/license background music for the two silent beats (0:00-0:03 intro montage, 1:00-1:10 feature montage), (4) assemble final cut.

2026-07-15: Revisited automated assembly (had been deferred in favor of manual editing per 2026-07-11 decision) to fix VO/footage sync drift at its root instead. Found and fixed TWO distinct causes, confirmed empirically via live captures, not just reasoning:
  1. Old design shared one continuous multi-minute Playwright recordVideo take across many clips, recovering each clip's boundaries via a per-file wall-clock scale factor. Drift wasn't uniform, so the linear correction missed real boundaries by 10+ seconds late in a take.
  2. First fix attempt: one Electron launch + one Playwright recordVideo file per clip. Still fundamentally broken: Playwright recordVideo is CDP-screencast-driven, only emits frames on repaint -- static holds (exactly what b-roll needs) produced videos 2-3x shorter than real wall-clock time.
  Real fix (implemented + verified via live --clip runs in docs/capture_broll.js, docs/marketing/assemble_reel.js, docs/marketing/build_reel.js): replaced Playwright recordVideo with ffmpeg's gdigrab (Windows OS-level real-time screen capture), scoped to the fullscreened Electron window's actual bounds via -offset_x/-offset_y/-video_size (bare 'desktop' grabs the whole virtual desktop -- confirmed on this 3-monitor dev box it produced 6400x2160 with the app in one corner). Capture starts only after clip.setup() has already navigated to the settled state, so the file IS the clip -- no offset math, manifest.json just records {file}. Verified: static clip duration matched wall-clock (5.16-5.20s actual vs ~5.0s expected), motion clip similarly accurate.
  Also added two requested b-roll beats: bigger/slower pan on the opening Project Canvas shot (dx:-550,dy:-230 vs old -300/-120), and Choices Canvas now jumps to stage1_arrival via the "Jump to Label" search box and clicks through 2 real choice pills via new clickChoicePills() helper to demonstrate walking a route progressively.
  Committed as 47d722f on release-v1-prep (not pushed).

2026-07-15 (same session, continued): ElevenLabs account hit its quota (10000/10000 credits, 2 remaining) on the first real full-pipeline run -- all 13 VO lines failed with 401 quota_exceeded, no credits actually spent (failed requests). User has an RTX 4090 locally, so replaced ElevenLabs with local Chatterbox TTS (Resemble AI, open-source) instead of waiting for quota reset:
  - New docs/marketing/chatterbox_generate.py: loads ChatterboxTTS once (~10-35s), generates all lines in one process (avoids per-line reload cost), emits `RESULT: {json}` lines to stdout for the Node wrapper to parse incrementally.
  - New docs/marketing/generate_vo_local.js: same parseScriptLines/output-contract as generate_vo.js (identical timing-summary.json/cue-sheet.csv shape, just .wav instead of .mp3) so assemble_reel.js and build_reel.js don't need to know which engine produced the audio.
  - Runs in an isolated venv at docs/marketing/.venv-chatterbox (gitignored) rather than the global/dev Python -- Chatterbox pins torch==2.6.0/torchaudio==2.6.0, which would otherwise fight the global torch 2.11 install. IMPORTANT GOTCHA: plain `pip install chatterbox-tts` silently pulls a CPU-only torch wheel even on this CUDA machine -- confirmed empirically (torch.cuda.is_available() was False after a clean install). Fixed via a forced reinstall with --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124. Any future venv rebuild must do the same two-step install or generation will silently run on CPU (much slower, though the code does still work either way -- device is auto-detected).
  - build_reel.js gained --vo-engine local|elevenlabs (default local); generate_vo.js (ElevenLabs) kept intact and selectable via --vo-engine elevenlabs once quota is available again.
  - Verified end-to-end for real: full 13-line VO generation via `node docs/marketing/build_reel.js --steps vo` completed in ~45s wall-clock on the RTX 4090 (10.6s model load + ~2.5-4.5s per line), 0 failures, valid 24kHz mono PCM wavs confirmed via ffmpeg, durations self-consistent.
  - Test artifacts (docs/marketing/vo/) cleaned up after verification -- not committed (gitignored, regenerable).

Remaining for the reel overall: full real end-to-end run (vo + all 22 broll clips + assemble) with the NEW local-VO + gdigrab-broll pipeline hasn't been done as one combined run yet -- only each piece individually. title: snippets: community snippet pack sharing (import/export collections)
description: Allow exporting a selection of snippets (or a full category) to a JSON file for sharing, and importing a shared pack. snippets/README.md and snippets/CHANGELOG.md both listed this as planned but unbuilt; consolidating into this one issue and removing those stale docs.
close_reason: Implemented full export/import for snippet packs. electron.js gained a narrowly-scoped snippets:* IPC namespace (readUserGlobal/writeUserGlobal against a fixed main-process-computed path, and exportPack/importPack which open native dialogs in the main process so the renderer never supplies an arbitrary write/read path) -- deliberately separate from the project-root-guarded fs:* handlers since custom.json lives outside any project root. Also fixed a latent bug: useSnippetLoader's step 2 (custom.json) previously went through fs:readFile/fileExists, which guardProjectPath (added in e7ab5b7) silently rejects with ACCESS_DENIED whenever a project is loaded, since userData is outside project root -- user-global snippets were effectively broken. Now reads via the new fixed-path IPC instead. SnippetGridView gained Select mode + per-snippet checkboxes + Export Selected/Export Category (writes a SnippetPackFile via new src/lib/snippetPackExport.ts, with a browser <a download> fallback). SnippetManager gained an Import Pack... button that validates the picked file with ny1's snippetSchema validator, merges it into custom.json via new src/lib/snippetPackMerge.ts (skips exact title+code duplicates), writes back, and reloads. 2113/2113 tests passing (36 new: 6 snippetPackMerge + 4 new SnippetGridView export tests + 4 new SnippetManager import tests + assorted loader test updates), tsc/eslint clean, electron.js/preload.js syntax-checked.

title: tree-sitter-renpy: property's dynamic precedence arbitrarily loses name/value split for identifier-valued screen properties
description: Found during the final whole-branch review's fix-wave re-review of bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i (2026-08-16). C3's fix added a lone-identifier alternative to property (grammar.js) via prec.dynamic(2, name-value pair) vs prec.dynamic(1, bare identifier), to make 'use other_screen'-style single-property lines parse. Side effect: when a property's VALUE is itself a bare identifier (e.g. 'vbox style mystyle:', 'button action Return() style ok', screen 'for i in range(10):'), the two dynamic-precedence weights sum equally across the alternative parse paths and the tie is broken arbitrarily -- these now sometimes parse as two/N separate bare 'property (expression)' nodes instead of one name/value pair. No ERROR node either way; real-file screens.rpy error counts still improved 619->152 with this in place. Nothing in src/ currently reads property's name/value fields (only the opaque expression content, via the Python-injection query), so no downstream consumer is affected today. Recommended when picked up: either accept as a documented grammar limitation (property's shape is not fully deterministic for identifier-valued name/value pairs), or replace the dynamic-precedence tie-break with an explicit lookahead/grammar restructuring that deterministically prefers the name-value pairing when a subsequent line begins a differently-indented block (matching the vbox/button/for corpus cases that still work correctly today by accident of test selection).

title: tree-sitter-renpy: parseBlock's dedent() only strips spaces, not tabs
description: Follow-up from bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 11 (parseBlock() API) code review, 2026-08-16. The multi-span python:/init python: block reconstruction algorithm's dedent() helper (src/lib/tree-sitter/parseBlock.ts) only strips literal space characters when re-indenting a reconstructed Python span. A tab-indented python: block body would not be dedented correctly, potentially producing a Python IndentationError on the reconstructed span handed to the injected tree-sitter-python parser. Ren'Py/this codebase's convention is space-indentation so this is unlikely to bite in practice, and no test currently exercises tab-indented python: blocks. Recommended fix when picked up: extend dedent() to handle tab characters (e.g. treat a tab as matching one indent unit, or detect/reject mixed tab/space indentation explicitly) if tab-indented .rpy files are ever found in the wild.

title: tree-sitter-renpy: document Docker requirement for building the grammar wasm
description: Follow-up from bmf-vangard-renpy-ide-qu9i Task 10 (build/bundling pipeline) code review, 2026-08-16. Building tree-sitter-renpy's compiled renpy.wasm (via the manual 'npm run build:grammar' script) requires Docker running locally in this environment (no emcc/podman present), since tree-sitter-cli falls back to a containerized emscripten build for the --wasm step. This is currently undocumented -- no README.md exists under tree-sitter-renpy/, and root README.md has no mention of build:grammar or the Docker/emcc requirement. A future contributor without Docker running would get a confusing failure when trying to edit the grammar and rebuild. Recommended fix: add a one-line note (in a new tree-sitter-renpy/README.md, or the root README's contributing section) documenting that editing grammar.js requires running 'npm run build:grammar' locally with either emscripten (emcc) or Docker available, and committing the resulting tree-sitter-renpy/renpy.wasm.
